        <div class="page-intro">
          <p class="lead">
            Explore our collection of research articles covering control-affine theory, biomechanics, and golf swing dynamics. The articles are organized by topic, from foundational theory to advanced applications.
          </p>
          <div class="callout-note" style="background: #f0f7ff; border-left: 4px solid #2563eb; padding: 1rem; margin: 1rem 0; border-radius: 4px;">
            <strong>Suggested Reading Path:</strong> Start with the <em>Drifter Manifesto</em> (Parts 1–3) for the core framework, then explore <em>Superposition in Affine Control Systems</em> and <em>Controllability and Drift–Control Ratio</em> for deeper analysis. The <em>Tangent Hyperplanes</em> series extends these ideas to general nonlinear systems. <em>Dynamics and Control of the Golf Swing</em> applies the full framework to the golf swing with graduate-level rigor. <em>Geometric Control of Nonlinear Systems</em> provides comprehensive mathematical foundations.
          </div>

          <div id="physics-of-golf" class="article-category">
            <h3 class="category-title">Dynamics and Control of the Golf Swing <span style="display: inline-block; margin-left: 0.5rem; padding: 0.15rem 0.5rem; background: #dcfce7; color: #166534; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; vertical-align: middle;">NEW</span></h3>
            <p class="category-intro">A comprehensive textbook on the biomechanics and control theory of the golf swing, covering 31 chapters across 10 parts&mdash;from double-pendulum models through the affine drift&ndash;control framework, constraint forces, musculoskeletal modeling, motor control, and impact dynamics. <a href="../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/index.html">View full book →</a></p>
            <div class="accordion-item">
              <button class="accordion-header" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
                <span>Part I &mdash; Foundations (Chapters 1&ndash;3)</span>
                <span class="accordion-icon">+</span>
              </button>
              <div class="accordion-content">
                <p>Why physics matters for golf, the language of motion (coordinates, configuration spaces), and the double-pendulum model of the golf swing.</p>
                <a href="../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/ch01_why_physics.html" class="resource-link">Start Reading →</a>
              </div>
            </div>
            <div class="accordion-item">
              <button class="accordion-header" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
                <span>Part II &mdash; The Affine Framework (Chapters 4&ndash;6)</span>
                <span class="accordion-icon">+</span>
              </button>
              <div class="accordion-content">
                <p>Forces and torques, the control-affine structure of the equations of motion, and the Zero-Torque Counterfactual (ZTCF)&mdash;the central analytical tool of the book.</p>
                <a href="../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/ch04_forces_and_torques.html" class="resource-link">Start Reading →</a>
              </div>
            </div>
            <div class="accordion-item">
              <button class="accordion-header" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
                <span>Parts III&ndash;IV &mdash; Constraints, Mechanisms, and Forces (Chapters 7&ndash;10, 15&ndash;17, 19, 28&ndash;29, 31)</span>
                <span class="accordion-icon">+</span>
              </button>
              <div class="accordion-content">
                <p>Constraint forces, the triple pendulum, parallel mechanisms, energy transfer, ground reaction forces, muscle mechanics, aerodynamic drag, impact collision dynamics, joint damping, and swing plane geometry.</p>
                <a href="../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/ch07_constraint_forces.html" class="resource-link">Start Reading →</a>
              </div>
            </div>
            <div class="accordion-item">
              <button class="accordion-header" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
                <span>Parts V&ndash;VII &mdash; Inverse Problems, Physical System, and Musculoskeletal Model (Chapters 11&ndash;12, 18, 20&ndash;23)</span>
                <span class="accordion-icon">+</span>
              </button>
              <div class="accordion-content">
                <p>Inverse dynamics, the flexible shaft, fascia, soft tissue mechanics, spine modeling, joint anatomy, degrees of freedom, and URDF models.</p>
                <a href="../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/ch18_inverse_dynamics_parallel.html" class="resource-link">Start Reading →</a>
              </div>
            </div>
            <div class="accordion-item">
              <button class="accordion-header" type="button" aria-expanded="false">
                <span>Parts VIII&ndash;X &mdash; Kinetic Chain, Motor Control, and Synthesis (Chapters 13&ndash;14, 24&ndash;27, 30)</span>
                <span class="accordion-icon">+</span>
              </button>
              <div class="accordion-content">
                <p>The kinetic chain and performance, motor control and the brain, motor learning, passive distributed control, and the complete integrated swing model.</p>
                <a href="../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/ch30_kinetic_chain.html" class="resource-link">Start Reading →</a>
              </div>
            </div>

          <div id="textbook-series" class="article-category">
            <h3 class="category-title">Geometric Control of Nonlinear Systems &mdash; Textbook Series <span style="display: inline-block; margin-left: 0.5rem; padding: 0.15rem 0.5rem; background: #fef9c3; color: #854d0e; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; vertical-align: middle;">IN DEVELOPMENT</span></h3>
